label: beodeul_city/capital/capital_dais

surfaces.part: flagstone platform top with rim stones and inlaid disc
front riser and step (light stone blocks)

answer.evidence: Rows 1-18 form a large flagstone top, with mortar lines and an inlaid blue and gold disc at rows 3-11. Row 19 is a dark front-edge line (L=63) across the width. Below it, rows 20-30 show a front riser of block courses with mortar joints, and a darker line at row 30 starts the step at row 31. The top is much taller than a rim and the front face is 3+ rows, so the main body has both a top surface and a front face. No isometric side face is drawn.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate shows 12 visible tones per 16x16 tile, against 7 for the paving reference and 3 for the grass. Near-flat coverage is 1%, so there are no large flat fills. The flagstone top has light, mid and shadow stones, with mortar joints and speckle. The rim stones and the front riser are separated by value steps, and the one-course riser and step read as distinct planes. The blue disc with the gold star adds extra tonal variety. The dark edge pixels are only 30% neutral, so most outlines lean toward a tint of the adjacent stone rather than a uniform black sticker line. Together with the reference paving's 80% neutral edges, this reads as mixed. Per-stone shading is a little simpler than the cobble detail in the paving reference, but with 27 colours in total it is at or above the reference on the primary facts. A careful artist could accept it next to the reference.
